headline: Every major sits under its 200-day line while ETF desks keep buying
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it settles most arguments before they start. All seven majors here, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, sit below their 200-day moving averages, and none shows a golden cross. That's a market that hasn't repaired its long-term trend, whatever the day's mood. Bitcoin is 49% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51, and the pain gets worse down the cap table: ADA is 83.2% off its high, DOGE 75.7%, SOL 70.4%. This is a still-broken tape structurally, even with a Greed reading on the sentiment gauge.

Momentum tells a more mixed story than trend does, and the mix itself is the finding. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, neutral, with MACD below signal, a market resting rather than trending. ETH's RSI is a firmer 56.3 and it's up 1.8% on the week and 6.4% on the month even while down 0.8% on the day, but its MACD is also below signal: momentum improving under the hood while the trend indicator hasn't confirmed it. BNB and DOGE show the opposite split, MACD above signal despite sitting below their 200-day lines and posting soft RSI readings (48.3 and 40.7). Nothing here is aligned top to bottom. That's a market working through conflicting signals, not one leaning hard in either direction.

Positioning is where the leverage crowd's temperature shows. Funding across the board is modest and positive, from BTC's 5.9% annualized to XRP's 11.0% and DOGE's 4.4%, meaning longs are paying shorts a small toll to stay in the trade. Not expensive, not crowded. But the long/short account ratios tell a different story by asset: DOGE at 3.54, XRP at 2.16, SOL at 1.74, all skewed heavily long relative to BTC's 1.11 and ETH's 1.21. And the liquidation tape over the last 24 hours backs that skew up: BTC longs lost $8.96M against $1.78M for shorts, ETH longs lost $11.63M against $3.05M for shorts, DOGE longs lost $2.57M against just $45K for shorts. Long positioning is getting punished more than short positioning across every asset with data. Crowded longs, cheap funding: a position that's fragile without being expensive.

Flows split cleanly by address type. The ETF bid remains firmly one direction: BTC funds took in $314.3M on 25 Aug, part of a $2,082.9M five-session net with 7 consecutive days in the same direction; ETH funds added $179.8M that day, $885.7M over five sessions, also 7 same-direction days. That's about as unambiguous as flow data gets. Whale wallets agree with the ETF desks for once: $119M net moved off exchanges in the last 24 hours, driven by BTC, with the single biggest move being $155.1M off Coinbase. Zoom out to the weekly cadence and the picture actually flips: three of the last four weeks (ending Aug 12, Aug 19, Aug 26) show net flows onto exchanges, including $990M onto exchanges in the week ending Aug 26. So today's daily whale print runs counter to the recent weekly trend, worth naming rather than smoothing over. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat, up just 0.34% over 30 days to $309.0B, no fresh firepower building on the sidelines.

Sentiment sits at 65, Greed, inside its 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is feeling good about a tape where every major is still under its long-term trend line and long positions are the ones getting liquidated. That gap between mood and structure is itself the read for today: enthusiasm is running ahead of the technical picture, funded by real ETF inflows but sitting on top of a market that hasn't reclaimed its 200-day lines anywhere.

What to watch: any asset reclaiming its 200-day average would be the first real crack in the broken-trend picture, a flip in BTC's or ETH's funding from positive to negative would signal the long crowd finally capitulating, and a shift in the weekly whale flow back toward off-exchange (matching today's daily print instead of contradicting it) would suggest cold storage accumulation is actually building rather than fighting the recent trend.
